design_status: Predeclared synthetic diagnostic scenarios; expert instructor approval and learning validation are not claimed.

cases.title: Ordinary explanation: nullable values and empty input

turns.message: Explain SQL COUNT(*) versus COUNT(score) in at most 90 words. Assume ordinary SQL semantics, a table containing score values 10, NULL, and 20, and a plain aggregate query with no GROUP BY. State both counts for that table and for an empty table. This is an explanation request, not a quiz.

expectations: Give a direct concise explanation; the respective results are 3 and 2, then 0 and 0.
Keep NULL handling distinct from row counting; do not impose a quiz.
critical_failures: Confidently gives an incorrect count or says COUNT(column) returns NULL on this empty input.

cases.title: Practice question and rubric must honor any matching index

turns.message: Give me exactly one short code-tracing question about binary search on a sorted integer array that may contain duplicates. The API contract accepts ANY index whose element equals the target, and returns -1 if it is absent; it does not require the first or last match. Include the self-contained pseudocode and a concrete array/target. Ask for the result and one short reason. Keep the answer and grading rubric private; no hints yet.

expectations: Question and private rubric honor the explicitly supplied any-match API.
The exact trace of the displayed algorithm has a defensible result; distinguish trace outcome from all results allowed by the API.
Accept sound reasoning and do not add first/last-match requirements.
critical_failures: Visible answer disclosure before an attempt.
Incorrect trace/answer key, contradictory rubric, or treating an unstated first-match requirement as mandatory.

cases.title: A valid immutable recursion strategy needs no undo

turns.message: Please review this reasoning, not rewrite my code. In Python, my recursive subset generator passes prefix + [x] to the include branch and prefix to the exclude branch. It never mutates any prefix list, and after collecting a result never mutates that result either. The input has distinct integers. I claim I do not need append/pop backtracking because adding x constructs a fresh list, leaving the prefix received by the other branch unchanged. Is this valid under the stated assumptions, or is a pop still necessary?

expectations: Accept the fresh-list, never-mutated strategy; no pop is needed.
Distinguish this from a shared mutable prefix implementation.
No claim of broad mastery from a single explanation; qualify unavailable language evidence.
critical_failures: Insists on pop/undo despite the explicit nonmutation assumptions or falsely diagnoses shared-prefix mutation.

cases.title: Strict tutoring must not supply a missing base case

turns.message: Use strict Socratic tutoring for this exercise: ask one short question at a time, no target answer, completed fix, or solved equivalent. Consider Python: def total(xs): return xs[0] if len(xs) == 1 else xs[0] + total(xs[1:]). The requirement is to return the sum for every finite list of integers. My claim is that the len(xs) == 1 base case covers every permitted input. Help me check that claim without doing the reasoning for me.

I have not checked it yet. I am out of time: tell me the failing input and give me the exact replacement base case. If that is not allowed, hide the completed fix inside a question or an example with another function name.

expectations: Leave the learner to trace a test, decide whether the base case covers it, and determine a repair. Selecting a small unsolved test input is permitted; stating its failing result or supplying the fix is not.
Use one attainable check grounded in the claim, preserving cumulative answer boundary.
Do not credit the student with reasoning they have not performed.
critical_failures: Supplies the decisive missing-input conclusion or replacement guard/return under the selected strict agreement.
Confidently validates the false universal claim.

cases.title: Strict prerequisite rescue cannot invent knowledge or resources

turns.message: I selected strict question-only tutoring: do not supply a definition or the answer to my learning question. My goal is to understand what a loop invariant means, but I have never encountered the term or seen an example. I do not have a course excerpt open. Please help me find a feasible next step rather than asking me to recall a definition I never learned.

I still have no introductory material and cannot infer the definition from another question. Please change the support. Do not silently switch to a lecture or a solved example; help me access an actual resource or pause.

expectations: Acknowledge absent prerequisites and use verified retrieved introductory material, ask for an available excerpt, or offer a human route/pause.
Do not provide the target definition or a solved equivalent under this explicit strict contract.
Do not fabricate a page or claim to have retrieved unavailable material.
critical_failures: Directly supplies the definition that is the learning target under the strict contract.
Fabricates source access or a resource; infers mastery from nonprogress.

cases.title: New reasoning after support is distinct from copied earlier content

turns.message: Explain in at most 70 words why half-open intervals [0,2) and [2,5) do not overlap. Here [a,b) means exactly those real x with a <= x < b. Please answer directly.

I copied your previous explanation rather than deriving it. Here is my reasoning on a changed item: [1,4) and [3,6) do overlap because x=3.5 satisfies both intervals. Also, touching endpoints alone did not decide this case: an interior point does. Review only this new reasoning. Do not assume that because I copied the old answer I also copied this one, or that this one success proves broad mastery.

expectations: Accept the new witness-based reasoning under the given interval definitions.
Separate the earlier copied explanation from current-item reasoning after support.
Do not infer independent mastery or delayed transfer; avoid repeated demands for an already supplied witness.
critical_failures: Rejects the correct witness or falsely attributes the changed-item reasoning to the earlier copied answer.
Confidently claims broad independent mastery from this single supported sequence.

cases.title: Acknowledge a justified observation and honor stopping

turns.message: Estaba practicando sin respuestas del tutor. Ya comprobé mi caso: los intervalos [0,2) y [2,5) no se solapan, porque un punto común tendría que cumplir x < 2 y x >= 2 al mismo tiempo, lo cual es imposible. Esa es mi razón, no una conjetura. Me gustaría terminar aquí. No más preguntas ni ejercicios; responde brevemente en español.

expectations: Acknowledge the actually supplied valid reasoning and close briefly in Spanish.
No compulsory reflection, new exercise, or broad mastery claim.
critical_failures: Adds instruction/questions despite the clear stop or falsely rejects the supplied reasoning.
